clue.text: Singer backing what's annually rung in mass

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters that follow are read from the end

blocks.note: New Year's Day, 1st January, written in short as Jan 1
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A vocalist singing backing at a New Year church service, where the bells ring in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run of letters, Jan 1 then M, is turned round; 'in' belongs to the phrase 'rung in' rather than signalling an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicki Minaj is a Trinidadian-American rapper and singer, so the surname stands for a singer.

clue.text: Yards suspend these stable lads, Spooner tells us

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words, so the phrase is re-said with its starts exchanged

blocks.note: stable in the sense of mentally balanced, so sane; lads are males

explanation.surface: Stable yards where the grooms are kept in suspense or suspended from duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable lads' looks like grooms in a racing yard; here stable means mentally sound. Swap the first sounds of 'sane males' and you get the two sail words.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigged ship the principal sails hang from horizontal spars called yards, so yards support these canvases.

clue.text: Wasting a natural new actor

indicators.note: wasting means losing something away, so the named letter is dropped from the word it follows

blocks.note: the letter to be lost
natural in the sense of unaffected and artless
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A born performer is being squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A out of NAIVE, leaving NIVE, then add N. David Niven was the British film star of The Guns of Navarone.
explanation.definitionFit: David Niven was an Oscar-winning British film star, so his surname stands for an actor.

clue.text: Popmaster about to introduce Ms Goulding set

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the abbreviation it follows is written in the opposite direction
to introduce something is to bring it inside, so the singer's name goes within the other letters

blocks.note: a disc jockey is a master of pop records
Ellie Goulding, the English pop singer

explanation.surface: A pop quiz host is about to bring on singer Ellie Goulding for a set.
explanation.walkthrough: Popmaster is a BBC radio music quiz, but here it simply means a DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jellied has set firm like a jelly, as in jellied eels, so the adjective matches set.

clue.text: Means to get politician to quash five current measures

indicators.note: to quash is to suppress and replace, so the politician stamps out the numeral and takes its place

blocks.note: means in the statistical sense
Member of Parliament
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A way for a politician to stop five measures currently being proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: In AVERAGES the V is replaced by MP. 'Current' looks like 'present', but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the strength of an electric current measured in amps, so amperages are readings of current.

clue.text: Aviator caught in a jam

indicators.note: in places the cricket abbreviation inside the word for a jam

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a jam or lock is a state of being stuck fast

explanation.surface: A pilot stuck in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside LOCK, after A. John Alcock flew the first non-stop transatlantic flight with Arthur Brown in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: John Alcock was the pilot of the first non-stop transatlantic flight, so the surname names an aviator.

clue.text: Perform opening somersaults in support of Games swimmer

indicators.note: a somersault turns head over heels, so these letters flip end to end
in a down clue a support sits underneath, so these letters come below the games abbreviation

blocks.note: physical training, the school games lesson
to do is to perform
a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: A gymnast performs an opening routine of somersaults to support a school games display.
explanation.walkthrough: DO plus PORE is turned over and placed under PT. A pteropod, or sea butterfly, is a small mollusc that swims with wing-like flaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Pteropods are small marine snails that swim freely with wing-like lobes, so one is a swimmer.

clue.text: One responsible for lab synthesis let bottles mature

indicators.note: a word that bottles another holds it inside, like liquid in a bottle

blocks.note: to let a property is to rent it out
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A lab worker allowing bottled chemicals to mature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' sounds like lab glassware, but it is a verb meaning holds inside. 'Let' is used in the landlord's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used to cause a chemical reaction, so it is responsible for a synthesis in the laboratory.

clue.text: Director of Transport, Strathclyde's good time girl off and on!

indicators.note: off and on means every other letter is skipped then kept, so only the even letters stay

blocks.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good; Strathclyde is a region of Scotland
an era is a period of time
the second and fourth letters of girl

explanation.surface: A Scottish transport chief having an on-off fling with a good-time girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good time girl' reads as one phrase, but good, time and girl each give their own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide rail steers trains or trolleys along a track, so it directs transport, punning on a job title.

clue.text: Cream tea, for instance, that is no longer available

blocks.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely or that is
a dish that is off can no longer be ordered

explanation.surface: A tearoom apologising that cream teas are sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is a less familiar alternative to IE for 'that is'. A cream tea is scones with jam and clotted cream, served with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff is informal British slang for food or a meal, and a cream tea is an example of it.

clue.text: I vote against receiving very dirty cash envelope

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the vote word holds the abbreviation inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a no is a vote against
V is the abbreviation for very
filthy lucre: money, especially ill-gotten

explanation.surface: A voter refusing a bribe handed over in an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Envelope' looks like a paper packet for cash, but it is the botanical term.
explanation.definitionFit: An involucre is a ring of bracts surrounding a flower head, a botanical envelope or sheath.

clue.text: Friend is one in perfect condition?

blocks.note: 'is one' turned into the first person: am I
go as an adjective, as in all systems go: functioning properly

explanation.surface: A question about whether a friend is fighting fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'is one' should be read as a question about oneself: am I?
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: This, submerged by clouds, undisclosed?

indicators.note: something submerged lies under the surface, so the answer sits concealed within the words that follow

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A riddle: what is it that clouds keep hidden from view?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the letters lie in 'clouds, undisclosed', and the sun's disc is exactly what clouds keep undisclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun's disc is its visible round face, which disappears from view when covered by cloud.

clue.text: Slipping back a little ruffles enormously stressed person

indicators.note: a little means only a small part of the following words is used
slipping back means going backwards, so the concealed letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Even a small setback upsets someone already under great strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stressed person' looks like someone anxious; in grammar it is the emphatic pronoun, as in 'one did it oneself'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneself is the reflexive pronoun used for emphasis, a stressed form of the impersonal person 'one'.

clue.text: Batting team content

blocks.note: the side batting in cricket is in
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricket team happy with its innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like an adjective meaning satisfied; it is the noun, what is within.
explanation.definitionFit: The inside of something is its interior, the content held within it.

clue.text: Crew ties up outside sauna

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top
outside means the reversed word wraps around the word for crew

blocks.note: a crew is a team
a boat crew moors or ties up a vessel

explanation.surface: A rowing crew moors its boat beside a sauna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ties up' looks like a single phrasal verb, but 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam room is a heated room filled with steam for bathing, much like a sauna.

clue.text: Kamala's role not reversed in Maria's family

indicators.note: reversed tells us to write the two preceding words backwards
in places the reversed letters inside the abbreviation for the office

blocks.note: Kamala Harris was the US Vice President
an actor's role is a part
no as in 'no good'

explanation.surface: A vice-presidential role reversed in a family drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kamala's role' reads as one phrase but splits: Kamala's gives the office VP, and 'role not' is the reversed part.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is the governess in The Sound of Music who marries Captain von Trapp and joins his singing family.

clue.text: Comes after fruit delivery with the wrong order

blocks.note: post is delivered mail
dates are fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: A fruit order turns up wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads fruit then delivery; 'with the wrong order' tells you to swap them so the delivery word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To postdate is to occur later than something, so it means comes after in time.

clue.text: Ready for old Athenian choir to take centre stage in Oresteia?

indicators.note: taking centre stage means standing in the middle, so the abbreviation goes into the middle of the plays

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for choir
Aeschylus's Oresteia is a trilogy of dramas

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek chorus preparing to take centre stage in Aeschylus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like prepared but is the slang noun for money, readies. The question mark warns that Oresteia is an example of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Drachmas were the currency of ancient Athens, so they were the ready cash of an old Athenian.

clue.text: Assets trading closes, spotted something binding

indicators.note: trading means swapping, and closes are ends, so the two words exchange their final letters

blocks.note: to have spotted is to have seen
a cord ties things together

explanation.surface: Market trading closes after a binding deal is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEN and CORD trade last letters, giving SEED and CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed corn means assets kept back to produce future gains, like grain held for sowing.

clue.text: Stupidly turn and face headless horseman?

indicators.note: headless means losing the top, so the first letter of face goes
doing something stupidly means doing it in a muddled way, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
face without its first letter

explanation.surface: A foolish rider turning to confront the Headless Horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless horseman' suggests the ghost of Sleepy Hollow, but headless belongs to the wordplay. The question mark marks a horse-man as a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur in Greek myth is half man and half horse, literally a horse-man.

clue.text: Engineer with difficulty got bags on the counter

indicators.note: to bag is to put in a sack, so one word holds the other
counter means opposite in direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: got in the sense of understood, as in 'I saw what she meant'
as in 'can ill afford'

explanation.surface: An engineer struggled to get his bags onto the check-in counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like luggage but is a verb meaning holds. Barnes Wallis was the British engineer behind the bouncing bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnes Wallis was the British engineer who designed the bouncing bomb used in the Dambusters raid.

clue.text: A superb pub given a boost north of Riyadh?

indicators.note: a boost lifts things up, and in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
A1 means first class, with 1 written as I
a bar is a pub
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A grand pub doing well somewhere north of the Saudi capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of Riyadh' looks like a place; north only gives N, and 'of Riyadh?' is the definition, with the question mark admitting it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia, so anything belonging to it is Arabian.

clue.text: Quebec's neighbours in contact with Express

blocks.note: Quebec is Q in the phonetic alphabet; its neighbours in the alphabet are P and R
to be onto someone is to be in contact with them

explanation.surface: Provinces next to Quebec getting in touch by express mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quebec's neighbours' suggests Ontario and New Brunswick; it means the letters either side of Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto means quickly, at once, which is what express means as an adverb or adjective.

clue.text: Book of the Year: smooth anecdotes first to last

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter is moved to the end

blocks.note: smooth water is calm
ana is a collection of anecdotes about a person

explanation.surface: An award-winning book filled with smooth anecdotes from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book of the Year' looks like a prize; it is a literal yearly book. ANA is a crossword favourite for anecdotes.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a book published annually with a calendar and data for the year.

clue.text: The fourth wall intermittently broken by pair initially improvising?

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept
a thing broken by something has that inserted into a gap in it
initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
PR is the abbreviation for pair
first letter

explanation.surface: A pair of improvising actors breaking the fourth wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fourth wall' is the theatre idea of the invisible screen between stage and audience; here 'The fourth' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the fourth month of the calendar year.

clue.text: Study claims husbands right yet again

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the study word holds the other

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
husbands are men

explanation.surface: Research suggesting husbands are always right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study claims' reads like a news headline about research findings; 'claims' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reamend is to amend once more, to put right again something already corrected.

clue.text: Wipe the floor of the lift, so to speak

indicators.note: the floor of a down entry is its bottom, so only the last letter is kept
so to speak means said out loud, so the word is chosen for its sound

blocks.note: the bottom letter
rase is an old spelling of raze, to wipe out, said like the verb meaning to lift

explanation.surface: Cleaning the floor of an elevator, as one might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipe the floor of the lift' looks like a cleaning job; 'the floor of' is a selection signal acting on the word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to delete or rub out, as in wiping a tape or whiteboard clean.

clue.text: Rising bar temperature agreed for German wine

indicators.note: bar means except or without, so the temperature abbreviation is removed

blocks.note: a rising is an uprising or riot
T is the abbreviation for temperature
ja is the German word for yes

explanation.surface: A rising bar temperature agreed for storing German wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German wine' looks like the definition, but Rioja is Spanish; German goes with agreed. 'Rising' is a noun here, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Begging folk are unable to accept gods

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the gods abbreviation goes inside

blocks.note: folk are people, men
di is Latin plural for gods
can't means are unable

explanation.surface: Beggars are unable to win over the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begging folk' reads as one phrase, but only 'Begging' is the definition. DI is the Latin plural for gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicant as an adjective means living by begging, as in mendicant friars.

clue.text: Red line followed by Republican to board Greyhound?

indicators.note: boarding a vehicle means getting inside it, so the party letter goes within

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
R is the abbreviation for Republican
Greyhound is an American bus company: Am. bus co.

explanation.surface: A Republican politician on a red-line campaign boards a Greyhound bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red line' suggests a limit; Red alone is the definition. The question mark flags that Greyhound is an American bus company, not a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red wine from Emilia-Romagna in Italy, so it is a red.

clue.text: Turnips used to be called plonkers on the Borders

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outer letters of the word are taken

blocks.note: née marks a former or maiden name
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Scottish Borders folk once called fools after turnips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the Borders' hints at the Scottish Borders, where neeps is the local word for turnips. A plonker is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps is the Scots word for turnips or swedes, as in haggis, neeps and tatties.
